title: Boise Foothills Access Road (Cottonwood Creek to Fivemile Creek)
description: A single-lane gravel access road with fire apparatus access through the Boise Foothills study corridor, from Mountain Cove Rd at E Cottonwood Creek Rd (start, about 2,830 ft) to Rocky Canyon Rd (Shaw Mountain Rd) at Fivemile Creek (end, about 3,820 ft) - about 990 ft of climb over 4 miles.

**Map source.** `boise-stitched-usgs-topo-layout2.pdf`, a 24 x 36 inch AutoCAD plot (rotated 270 degrees) of three stitched USGS topo tiles with a translucent green study corridor and magenta start and end dots. The page was rendered at 200 dpi without the corridor and dots (`map.png`); the corridor was rendered separately as a mask. The scale bar measures 3,317 px = 10,000 ft (matching the PDF's 8.37 ft per point measure). North is up (map-up assumed north).

**Contour intervals.** The lower tile (south of the horizontal seam) has 20 ft contours with 100 ft index contours; the two upper tiles have 40 ft contours with 200 ft index contours. The grid preview and plots draw 40 ft contours. The lower-right corner of the sheet has no tile (no elevation data) and is outside the study corridor.
**Study corridor.** The land outside the green corridor is modeled as two exclusion areas, so every option stays within the corridor.

**Digitizing.** Contours were traced by color (thin light-brown and dark-brown index contours, with trails, grid lines, and text rejected), split at the tile seams. Index contour elevations were read from the printed labels and followed across gaps by hand; the intermediate contours were labeled by fall-line rays between labeled contours (a contour is labeled only when several rays agree), plus transects in the start valley and on the Bucktail Trl bench. Stream bed spot elevations (from where the labeled contours cross each stream) keep the narrow creek bottoms from filling in. The topography grid is 50 ft (418 x 128 cells). About 1,100 of 1,800 traced contour pieces are labeled - nearly all within the corridor; the rest are short fragments or outside the corridor.

**Design criteria.** Single-lane gravel residential / rural access road with fire apparatus access (assumed): 14 ft wide, 12% maximum grade (designed at 11%), 50 ft minimum radius, 1:1 cut and 1.5:1 fill slopes, turnouts every 400 ft or less.

**Existing roads.** Rocky Canyon Rd (a graded road along Cottonwood Creek) reaches the end point. The options join it and follow it to the end, costed at the existing road upgrade rate. Its width, grade, surface, and condition are unknown and not checked against the criteria.

**Options considered and dropped.** An all-new road that parallels Rocky Canyon Rd to the end (cost score about 3,500) is more expensive than joining the road and crosses Cottonwood Creek more than 20 times in the narrow canyon bottom. Routes that stay north of Rocky Canyon along the 3,800-4,000 ft slopes cost 6,000-7,000+ with deep cuts and walls on 50-60% side slopes.
**Limitations.**

- Contours were machine-traced from a 1:24,000-scale map (accuracy about half a contour interval, 10-20 ft); the grid smooths features narrower than about 150 ft. Verify with a site survey before design.

- Along Rocky Canyon Rd the narrow canyon is narrower than the grid can represent, so the grid's grade along the existing road is approximate (it shows local pitches of 13-20% where the road's true average grade is about 5%).
- The contours are broken at the tile seams; the grid interpolates across them. Part of the new road runs along the horizontal seam (stations 120+00 to 135+00).
- Trails (Central Ridge, Bucktail, Ridge Crest, Three Bears) are not modeled as features; the new road crosses and partly follows them.
- Property lines, easements, utilities, geology (rock), and wetlands are not mapped; no rock excavation is assumed.
- The road connects two existing roads (a through route), so no dead-end turnaround is modeled; if Rocky Canyon Rd is gated, a fire apparatus turnaround is needed at the gate.

start.label: Start: Mountain Cove Rd at E Cottonwood Creek Rd

end.label: End: Rocky Canyon Rd at Fivemile Creek (Shaw Mountain Rd)

options.name: Rocky Canyon Rd Junction

structures.name: Drainage south of the tongue culvert

description: **Recommended.** New road from Mountain Cove Rd up the Central Ridge Trl valley, across the Bucktail Trl bench and the head of the drainage south of the 3,400 ft tongue, over the ridge at about 3,510 ft (station 130+00, along the tile seam), then down the northwest wall of Rocky Canyon to join Rocky Canyon Rd at station 143+10 (about 3,410 ft, where the canyon bends northeast). It follows Rocky Canyon Rd 7,970 ft up Cottonwood Creek to the end.
- About 14,310 ft of new construction at an 11% maximum grade; cut and fill are mostly under 10 ft. Stations 40+00 to 100+00 follow gentle ground (side slopes mostly under 15%).

- The descent into Rocky Canyon (stations 135+00 to 143+00) sidehills a 50-65% slope with up to 50 ft of cut on the uphill side and a short 5 ft retaining wall at 137+16 - the most difficult section; verify slope stability and rock in the field.
- Fill exceeds cut (about 16,000 cy of borrow) - the deepest fills (up to 28 ft) are at the drainage heads near stations 85+00 and 102+00.
- Culverts at Freestone Creek, the drainage south of the tongue, the Cottonwood Creek crossing at the junction, and the profile sags; 35 turnouts.
- Rocky Canyon Rd's condition is unknown: confirm its width (widening to 14 ft plus turnouts), grade, surface, and legal access before relying on it.

options.name: Curlew Gulch
description: Same start as the recommended option to the Bucktail Trl bench (station 55+00), then north into Curlew Gulch and up the gulch bottom to its head, over the spur at about 3,650 ft (station 145+00), and down the north wall of Rocky Canyon to join Rocky Canyon Rd at station 174+36 (about 3,560 ft). It follows Rocky Canyon Rd 4,940 ft to the end.
- About 17,440 ft of new construction at an 11% maximum grade - 3,100 ft more than the recommended option, but 3,000 ft less of the existing road.
- The gulch bottom section crosses Curlew Gulch (intermittent) 10 times - each needs a culvert; consider moving the alignment onto one bank in final design.

- The spur crossing has 40-45 ft cuts and fills (stations 133+00 to 146+00), and the descent along the north wall of Rocky Canyon (stations 150+00 to 166+00) sidehills 60-67% slopes with retaining walls up to 8 ft high on the downhill side.

- About 69% more costly than the recommended option (more earthwork, about 30,000 cy of borrow, walls, and culverts). Choose it only if the lower 3,000 ft of Rocky Canyon Rd can't be used or the canyon-mouth sidehill proves unstable.
